verified.title: run.py retry leaves last.prev/ and last.tmp/ behind, so "start fresh" silently resumes the old checkpoint (and can wedge the run)
verified.evidence: Commit 2a9e2a1 (2026-09-20) changed the trainer's resume checkpoint to a rename swap: `train/utils/trainer.py:78-96` (`_save_last`) writes into `last.tmp/`, renames the current `last/` to `last.prev/`, renames `last.tmp/` to `last/`, then removes `last.prev/`. A kill inside that window leaves `last.tmp/` or `last.prev/` on disk. `run.py:714-727` (`_clear_continue_markers`, what `run.py retry` calls at run.py:739) deletes only `done.json`, `consumed.json`, `train_log.jsonl`, `train_done.json`, `align_check.json` and `last/`. Nothing deletes `last.prev/` or `last.tmp/`. On the next launch `train/utils/trainer.py:99-107` (`_settle_last`, called at trainer.py:175 before the resume branch at trainer.py:183) renames `last.prev/` back to `last/`. The two documents carry the same gap: `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:210-213` lists exactly the six names run.py deletes, and `README.md:252`'s `writes:` line for `train/utils/trainer.py` still reads "best/, last/, train_log.jsonl, align_check.json, train_done.json, predictions.parquet, consumed.json, heartbeat, done.json" — commit 2a9e2a1 touched only trainer.py, jobs/RESULTS.md and jobs/runs.jsonl, so the README line was never updated for the two new directories.
verified.consequence: A train piece killed during a checkpoint write leaves `last.prev/`. The operator types `run.py retry train_probe <setting> train`, gpu-run Phase 6b tells them this is "start fresh", and the relaunched run instead resurrects `last.prev/` as `last/` and resumes from the pre-kill step — with `train_log.jsonl` deleted, so the log starts mid-training and the two halves cannot be joined. Worse, if a commit landed between the kill and the retry, `trainer.py:189-191` raises `recorded commit <x> differs from this run's commit <y>; run.py retry to start fresh` on every launch, and retry cannot clear the state it names: the run directory is wedged and only a hand `rm -rf` of `last.prev/` frees it, which is exactly the kind of by-hand surgery the skill exists to prevent.
verified.proposed_fix: In `run.py:_clear_continue_markers`, remove `last.tmp/` and `last.prev/` alongside `last/` for the train stage (one loop over the three names). Then widen `README.md:252`'s `writes:` line to name `last.tmp/` and `last.prev/`, and `.claude/skills/gpu-run/SKILL.md:210-213` and :223-224 to list them among what retry deletes.

            if p.exists():

refuted.title: A finish row contradicted by the run's own done.json can never be corrected: sync skips closed runs and the walk's backfill skips runs that are not open
refuted.reason:
The two gates are real, but they are the specified design, the documentation the finding calls contradictory actually agrees with the code, a correction path exists, and the live instance is already recorded in a ticket's Comments.

1. The code matches the contract that governs it. notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:4457-4465 (section 8.2) enumerates the five and only five writers of a finish row: "when a walk first sees `done.json` without a finish row (`ok`); when `run.py kill` ends a run (`killed`); when `jobs/launch.launch` returns anything but `up` ... (`launch_failed`); when `run.py sync` finds a run with no `done.json` **whose pieces `judge` calls `dead`** (`failed`); and when a stage `run.py` started in place exits non-zero (`failed`)." None of the five is "replace a finish row that is already there." `_backfill_finish_row`'s `open_runs()` test (run.py:1759-1761) is literally "a walk first sees done.json **without** a finish row", and `sync()`'s `entry["finish"] is not None` skip (jobs/registry.py:1072-1075) is the same sentence. The contract's other rule the finding could lean on — "`run.py` appends a new finish row whenever `done.json`'s `finished_at` is later than the newest finish row" (contracts:4495-4498) — is written for the always-recompute stages, and errata wave-5 item (b) rules exactly how it is realized: `eval` and `score` never take the skip (ALWAYS_RECOMPUTE, run.py:1969-1970), so they relaunch and append their own row. `train` is not one of them. So this is a request to change the contract, which is the owner's file and the owner's call, not a code defect.

2. The README citation is a misreading, not a contradiction. README.md:399-401 says `run.py sync` "folds any run directory's `done.json` and heartbeat files into a finish row **the ledger is missing**". The ledger is not missing a row here, so sync doing nothing is what that sentence describes. The finding quotes this as proof the docs promise something the code cannot do; it promises the opposite.

3. "Can never be corrected" is false. `run.py retry` (run.py:730-740) calls `_clear_continue_markers` (run.py:714-726), which unlinks `done.json` and, for train, `last/`, `train_log.jsonl`, `train_done.json`, `align_check.json`, then relaunches; the new start row clears the stale finish row in `fold` (jobs/registry.py:359-377, errata wave-7 item (f)), and the relaunch appends its own `ok`. The correction costs a recomputation, which is a real cost, but the mechanism exists. That `retry` cannot address a `--debug` run — the reason this particular row could not be fixed that way — is already an open errata item ("wave-6 close, open for the owner: kill / refire / retry take no --debug and cannot address a --debug run; contracts 8.6 pins their argv").

4. The live instance is already in the record. .scratch/from-zero/issues/18-migration-legacy-gitignore-timeline.md:350-352: "The ctool train row `train-0f3e343f0eca` reads `launch_failed` in `jobs/RESULTS.md` although the run finished with a `done.json`: the 30-second alive window closed it while it ran, and no later start row follows that finish row." That last clause is the mechanism itself, at the `fold` level. The producing cause is fixed (errata, section-4 walks, item (c): `alive_check` now returns on all up, on the first down, or at `launch_timeout_s`), and `jobs/launch.launch` calls `teardown_launch` before returning any non-`up` outcome (jobs/launch.py:900-909, 1071-1074), so a `launch_failed` row is now accompanied by the sessions actually being ended — the recurrence the finding predicts needs a teardown that loses the race with a finishing process, which is the residual of an already-recorded item rather than a new one.

5. The proposed fix is not implementable as written and would corrupt the ledger. A finish row's fields are fixed by contracts 8.2's table (`ev`, `t`, `run_id`, `status`, `counts`, `metrics`, `report`, `elapsed_s`) and by `append_finish`'s callers — no launch ordinal is recorded. So "the newest finish row is not the `ok` row for that same launch" cannot be evaluated by any reader. Dropping sync's `entry["finish"] is not None` skip and keeping only `done.get("launch") == _launch_ordinal(run_dir)` (jobs/registry.py:1089) matches the normal state of every completed run, so `run.py sync` would append a duplicate `ok` row for every finished run on every invocation.

What I would leave for the owner, not as a finding: after the walk skips a stage on a `done.json` whose `finished_at` is later than the newest finish row, no writer reconciles the two, so a wrong `launch_failed` / `failed` / `killed` row stands in `jobs/RESULTS.md` until someone spends a recomputation on `retry`. Closing that means adding a sixth writer to contracts 8.2 and a launch stamp to the finish row so a corrective row can be told from a duplicate.

refuted.title: A CPU stage's child process starts before its launches entry exists, so its done.json can stamp the previous launch ordinal and sync can then never close the run
refuted.reason:
The ordering the finding describes is real, but it is already a recorded, deliberately accepted assumption of the very commit the finding cites, and the consequence it claims is not reachable.

1. Already recorded and accepted. /home/y-guo/reproduce/new1/.scratch/from-zero/sdd/2026-09-20-wave7/walk-fixes-fix.json:94 is the fix record for the registry group whose head is 977210d — the commit that added done.json's `launch` field. Its third `concerns` entry is this finding, with the same file:line pair: "Ordering assumption, theoretical: for a CPU stage run.py spawns the process (run.py:1912) before it appends the `launches` entry (run.py:1937), both inside one lock hold. A child that wrote `done.json` within those microseconds would stamp the previous ordinal and read as stale, leaving the run open for the dead-piece test. A build/eval/score process cannot start its interpreter, read its inputs and finish in that window, and the failure direction is the safe one (no fabricated `ok` row)." The wave records under .scratch/from-zero/sdd/ are a named source of truth for this pass, so this is a re-report of an accepted item.

2. The reachability evidence does not measure the right thing. The child loses the race only if it reaches registry.write_done before the parent finishes /home/y-guo/reproduce/new1/run.py:1947. The child's floor is a cold interpreter plus the polars/schema/registry import layer: `time external/probe-env/bin/python run.py --help` measures 0.518 s real on this machine, and run.py imports the same layer the three CPU programs do (eval/utils/probe_eval.py:10 and eval/score_run.py:17 both `import polars as pl`). The parent's window is a few milliseconds of home-disk work: two dict literals, `registry.append_start` (append one line to a 102-line jobs/runs.jsonl plus `render()`, which formats those rows and writes RESULTS.md, jobs/registry.py:386-412), then `registry.write_meta`. The cited 0.11 s between two beats in outputs/debug/eval/f343c9118516/heartbeat/0-0.jsonl is the gap between two beats inside an already-running child, not the child's time from exec to done.json, so it does not show the window can be beaten.

3. The harmful outcome needs a second coincidence on top of the first. If the parent survives it writes the finish row itself at run.py:2068 and nothing is lost, so the run stays open only if run.py dies between run.py:1947 and run.py:2068 — and in the raced scenario the child has already exited, so `proc.wait()` (run.py:2059) returns at once and that window is milliseconds, not the duration of the stage.

Two corrections to the finding's own text, for the record. (a) Its consequence paragraph is wrong about the dead-piece branch: registry.judge (jobs/registry.py:682-687) tests `piece.get("status") == "done"` before `alive is False`, and `_piece_verdict_dict` fills that status from the last beat (jobs/registry.py:762-771), which Heartbeat.finish writes as "done" (jobs/registry.py:315-317). A finished cpu piece therefore reads `done`, the `all(v == "dead")` test at jobs/registry.py:1108 is false, and sync appends no row at all rather than a wrong `failed` row. (b) "Can never close" is narrower than stated: for build the next walk takes the skip path and `_backfill_finish_row` (run.py:1744-1769) closes the run on `finished_at`, and for eval/score the next walk always recomputes and appends a new start row that supersedes the open one in `fold`.

Not in dispute: the CPU path records the launch after the process that reads it has started, while the card path does the opposite (jobs/launch.py:1053-1065 appends the start row and the launches entry before any tmux session starts), and jobs/registry.py:248-253 reads the ordinal with no lock while the parent holds it. If the owner wants the asymmetry closed anyway, the finding's reorder is the right shape — write `launches=[launches_entry]` before the Popen in `_start_cpu_stage` (it needs only `git`, `_login_host()` and `argv_cmd`, all available there) and leave the pieces/pid write and the start row after the spawn; the one side effect is that a Popen that raises leaves a launches entry with no start row, which sync ignores because sync only looks at run_ids with an open start row.
